Title: Closing Remarks - Stakeholder Consultation Workshop on the Draft Policy Paper on the Proposed Financial Stability Framework
text: Closing Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles And Chairperson of the Financial Stability Committee Stakeholder Consultation Workshop on the Draft Policy Paper \on the Proposed Financial Stability Framework Thursday 28th April, 2022 Savoy Resort and Spa Members of the Financial Stability Committee, Second Deputy Governor, Participants, We have come to the end of an engaging and fruitful morning. I am encouraged to have witnessed the interactions amongst participants coming from different institutions as well as the frank and constructive views brought forward as we endeavour to achieve a common goal. I am confident that all stakeholders are leaving this forum having a deeper understanding of why financial stability is important and where we currently stand regarding having a country framework that is at par with global standards and adapted to the specificities of Seychelles. More importantly, todays exercise should provide more clarity on what needs to be done to address the various deficiencies identified, as well as the priority areas 1 that would need to be tackled to enhance financial stability and ensure that the country achieves its inclusive and sustainable growth objectives. As highlighted in my opening remarks, we all have a crucial role to play and this message should be taken back to our respective organisations and colleagues in anticipation of further discussions to finalise the proposed framework as this is certainly not a one-off undertaking. The valuable contribution of all stakeholders going forward will ensure that we have a framework that is comprehensive, inclusive and robust. The finalised policy document should be ready for presentation to the Cabinet of Ministers in the second quarter of the year. It is my sincere hope that this dynamism and collaborative approach will be maintained and strengthened not only to finalise the framework but to also ensure that we continue to remain abreast of developments that will assist in keeping it relevant for the benefit of our financial system and the wider economy. Global and domestic developments indicate that financial stability will have to remain at the forefront of our efforts to ensure our countrys economic stability and growth. To conclude, I would like to once again thank all the participants for your active engagement in this workshop. I wish to reiterate that we are only at the beginning of a very long journey, which will assist us in being able to have a more stable and resilient financial system that is conducive to inclusive and sustainable growth despite any uncertainties that our economy will face in the future. Thank you and I wish you all a pleasant afternoon, nice weekend and happy labour day. 2

Title: Welcoming Remarks by Governor Caroline Abel - 12th African Financial Inclusion Policy Initiative and 8th Pacific Islands Regional Initiative Meetings
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor Central Bank of Seychelles and Chairperson of the African Financial Inclusion Policy Initiative 12th African Financial Inclusion Policy Initiative (AfPI) and 8th Pacific Islands Regional Initiative (PIRI) Leaders Roundtable Savoy Resort and Spa, Seychelles Thursday 29th June 2023 Secretary of State for Finance, National Planning and Trade, Mr Patrick Payet, Executive Director, Alliance for Financial Inclusion, Dr Alfred Hannig, Governor of the Central Bank of Samoa and Chairperson of the Pacific Islands Regional Initiative, Ms Maiava Atalina Ainuu-Enari, Governors and Deputy Governors of AFPI and PIRI Central Banks, Members of the AFI Management Unit, Distinguished guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning. It is an honour to welcome you to Seychelles for the 12th AfPI and 8th PIRI Leaders Roundtable meetings, the first convergence meeting of these two groupings. Our geography should not limit our associations. In fact, the inclusion agenda compels us to find ways to expand beyond our traditional horizons and find innovative ways to build meaningful connections. The dual membership of Seychelles in the African and Pacific regional groupings, thanks to our African heritage and island specificities makes us an ideal point of convergence and we are grateful to AFI for recognising this trait and for facilitating the gathering of our two groups. Those of you who have had the chance to experience the sights and sounds of Mahe will identify with the tropical vibes so similar to our island colleagues and the African elements that come through our cuisine and music, entwined in our traditions. These facets have created a unique people and culture that allow us to bridge the differences and find similarities across PIRI and AfPI. It is hoped that the networks that you build while experiencing what Seychelles has to offer, will uncover many opportunities for collaborative growth. As we deal with the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic and navigate the various economic challenges resulting from other emerging global uncertainties, such as the Russia-Ukraine conflict, our aim for this meeting is for us, as financial inclusion leaders, to focus on how we prepare to respond to future eventualities in a proactive manner. The theme for the meetings, Rising above global uncertainty - pathways through inclusive innovation is therefore very fitting, given the current climate in which we are compelled to operate, as it prompts us to reflect on innovative policies that will not only help us navigate uncertainties, but also, to highlight the importance of continuity. Despite the geographic differences between our two regions, we share similar concerns and challenges. Disruptions to supply chains; inflation; climate change adaptation and adoption of green financing; economic slowdown due to the pandemic; the need to enhance consumer protection; I could continue with the list, to which I know as leaders, we can all relate. However, the theme for this meeting calls upon us to be active participants and propose tangible solutions that will build the resilience of our economies. With so much uniting us, I am confident that our shared values and aspirations will lead to fruitful discussions that will translate into innovative policies that will enhance the financial inclusion of our citizens. Thank you.

text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor - Central Bank of Seychelles & Chair of the African Financial Inclusion Policy Initiative (AfPI) AfPI Leaders Meeting Manila, Philippines Wednesday 13th September 2023 Dr Alfred Hannig, Executive Director of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion, Governors, Deputy Governors and Heads of Institutions Ms Malado Kaba, Director of the Gender, Women and Civil Society Department of the African Development Bank, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good afternoon. I am honoured to welcome you to this AfPI Leaders meeting, being held in the margins of the Global Policy Forum. It was not long ago that we had our Leaders Roundtable in Seychelles, but I am sure you will all agree that every opportunity that we get to meet, allows us to take stock of the initiatives being carried out in our region, assess their status and propose areas of improvement. Title: Opening Remarks by Governor Caroline Abel - CBS Board-Management Retreat 2023
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles CBS Board and Management Retreat Wednesday 8 - Thursday 9 November 2023 Venue: Savoy Resort & Spa Fellow Board Directors, Esteemed Colleagues from the International Monetary Fund, Members of Management, CBS Colleagues, Good morning. It gives me great pleasure to welcome you all today for the third Board and Management Retreat. Since our last retreat in 2020, the composition of our Board has seen some changes. Two Board Directors moved on from their roles - one to take up a new responsibility in the banking sector and the other having arrived at the end of his tenure - and we welcomed two new members amongst our ranks, notably First Deputy Governor Brian Commettant and Board Director James Jean, who were both previously members of the CBS Management team. The Management Team saw some additional movements, with four members choosing to pursue their careers outside of the Bank and six new staff members being promoted to lead their respective teams. We see these movements as a positive sign, a testament to the opportunities our staff are exposed to, whether it be to contribute their expertise to the broader economy or to bring renewed impetus to the work we are engaged in. The first Board and Management retreat held in 2018 formally laid the foundation for the development of the Strategic Plan 2019-2023, and our meeting held the following year was an opportunity to take stock of our achievements, discuss the challenges that we faced and check our compass to stay the course towards the achievement of our strategic goals. This meeting is, therefore, fitting as we near the completion of the current strategic cycle and finalise the strategies for the next. At this point, I would like to acknowledge our colleagues from the IMF who have responded positively to our request for technical assistance. The support encompasses remote consultations and desk reviews of documents prepared, and we are looking forward to the presentation dedicated to strategic planning later on today. I am sure that the expertise and insights that they will share with us over the next two days will be invaluable to ensure that we are on a path that is aligned with best practices and will allow us to refine the work that we have started. As we stand at the cusp of our 45 th Anniversary, the theme chosen for our new strategic plan - A progressive central bank: fostering sustainable economic transformation - aptly embodies our aspiration as we head towards our Golden Jubilee. The Central Bank is increasingly becoming central to the wider economy, moving beyond the traditional confines of the financial sector. Defining our new strategic priorities to respond to arising needs and developments while ensuring the delivery of our core mandates has been no easy 2 feat. I would like to thank the Strategic Planning Team being led by our Second Deputy Governor, who has played a pivotal role in outlining the plan that we will be refining and finalising over coming days. This is the core team that will lead the implementation of our new strategic plan, and the work that they have done over the past few months to define what success will look like in five years is commendable. Progress, however, cannot happen in isolation. Over the next two days, we will benefit from the external perspective of the IMF Team on a range of issues, including central bank governance and transparency, our legal framework, risk management and internal audit. It is anticipated that this exercise will better situate our current efforts and highlight opportunities, as well as areas for improvement, which should place us on the right footing as we move into our next five-year strategic cycle. Although we each have our individual roles to play, we must acknowledge that we have a collective responsibility to make a positive impact not only within CBS but in the broader economy and the lives of every member of the population which we are here to serve. I am looking into the foreseeable future with much enthusiasm, and I count on each and every one of you to contribute your best ideas to our discussions, to ensure that the initiatives that we take onboard inform sustainable and inclusive policies that will ultimately allow us to deliver on our mandates of price and financial stability. May this be a successful retreat. Thank You. 3

Title: Opening Remarks - AML-CFT Webinar for Seychelles Authorities
text: Closing remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Deputy Governor and Chairman of the Investment Committee of the Central Bank of Seychelles at the High Level Investment Forum 23 February 2018 Venue: Central Bank - Training Room Deputy Governor Daniel Mminele, Colleagues from the World Bank Treasury, Mr Bernard Murira and Mr Alessandro Caillat, Fellow members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Members of the Investment Committee, Central Bank staff, We have arrived at the close of this High Level Investment Forum. It has been a great opportunity to learn and share experiences as decision makers in the area of international reserves management. We had a dense and stimulating programme over these past two days and I am sure that the Board and Investment Committee members have some invaluable takeaways from the discussions. At this juncture, I would like to extend our sincere gratitude to our distinguished presenters; Deputy Governor Mminele, Mr Murira and Mr Caillat, for taking the time off their demanding schedules to travel to Seychelles and provide us with guidance and insight, as we navigate the continuously changing landscape of global investment. In the same vein, we are thankful for the assistance provided by the World Bank Treasury through the Reserves Advisory and Management Program. Seychelles officially joined RAMP in June 2015 and since then, we have made some great strides in improving staff capacity and toughening our reserves management framework. Even so, work remains as we strive to further develop the reserves management framework in its entirety. In line with this commitment, earlier in the week Mr Caillat conducted a series of workshops with the objective to provide guidance and equip staff with knowledge for the implementation of an operational risk management framework for reserves management activities. Mr Caillat, I would like to extend to you a special note of thanks for your generous assistance. I would also like to extend sincere appreciation for the participation of Deputy Governor Mminele of the South African Reserve as well as to Mr Murira for his invaluable assistance provided to the Central Bank throughout this process. Knowledge imparted through the sharing of experiences is one of the best means of teaching. To conclude, I would like to thank you all for your active participation in this High Level Investment Forum and take this opportunity to wish our guests a pleasant homebound journey. Thank you.

text_original: Ladres par Manmzel Caroline Abel Gouverner Labank Santral Sesel Alokazyon Anniversary Lecture 2018 Le 9 Novanm 2018 Sant Konferans Enternasyonal (ICCS) Speaker Lasanble Nasyonal, Prezidan Lakour Dapel, Minis, Sekreterdeta, Sekreter Prensipal, Manm Board, Management e Staff Labank Santral, Envite Distenge, Msye, Madanm, Manmzel, Bonswar. I fer mwan en tre gran plezir pour swet zot tou labyenveni pour nou Anniversary Lecture ki pe ganny fer a lokazyon 40tyenm laniverser Labank Santral Sesel. Le premye Desanm 1978, Lotorite Moneter Sesel ti ganny formen apre ki gouvernman ti war nesesite pour annan en tel lenstitisyon. Sa pa desisiv ti vin apre ki Sesel tin vin en pei endepandan e donk, responsab pour zer tou laspe son lekonomi lo li menm. Sepandan, fondasyon pour en tel lenstitisyon tin ganny mete depi byen lontan. 2 Rikord i montre ki an 1936 ti deza annan demars pour etablir en sistenm banker pli organize atraver en Komisyon Moneter, parey dan bann lezot koloni angle. Lo konmansman, rol sa Komisyon ti prensipalman pour zer lanmonnen ki ti an sirkilasyon Sesel sa letan, e pli tar, i ti osi responsab pour zer rezerv eksteryer pei. Pandan sa kat dernyen deseni, rol Labank Santral in evolye pour enkli plizyer fonksyon ki fer li en lenstitisyon kle dan developman ekonomik nou pei. Anmezir ki lekonomi i devlope e pas atraver bann sanzman striktirel, Labank Santral i bezwen adapte pour asire ki i reste azour avek sa bann devlopman e moderniz lafason ki i fonksyonnen. Dan sa konteks, i annan bokou sanzman kin arive pandan sa dernyen dizan. Avek liberalizasyon nou lekonomi, kot marse in vin pli ouver, lafason fer keksoz in osi bezwen sanze. Labank Santral in revwar son bann polisi e in entrodwir plizyer regilasyon pour asire ki nou sistenm banker i reste stab e anliny avek bann standar enternasyonal. Nou viv dan en lemonn ki deplizanpli konnekte e sak aksyon ki nou pran i kapab annan reperkisyon lo nou menm ou lezot nou bann partener. Fodre note ki i responsabilite sakenn de nou, sirtou bann ki angaze dan sistenm finansyel, pour fer sir ki nou sofgard nou repitasyon, an sort ki nou akse avek bann sistenm peyman enternasyonal i ganny mentenir. Depi 2009, lobzektif prensipal Labank Santral i pour promouvwar stabilite dan pri lo marse domestik. Pour kapab fer sa, nou bezwen reste vizilan anver bann devlopman dan lekonomi, sirtou bann ki annan potansyel pour 3 menas nou lobzektif. I dan sa laliny ki nou pe moderniz lafason ki nou enplimant polisi moneter, kot nou pou met plis lanfaz lo bann sinyal ki nou donn bann labank komersyal vizavi direksyon ki to lentere i sipoze bouze. Nou swete ki sa i ava ede pour konsolid sekter finansyel konman enn bann pilye nou lekonomi. Labank Santral i osi konsyan ki ledikasyon finansyel i en laspe tre enportan, si nou anvi asire ki nou bann polisi i ganny transmet e aplike efektivman. Noun osi realize, atraver plizyer sondaz, ki piblik pa neseserman konpran nou bann fonksyon ek rol ki nou zwe dan lekonomi. Se pour sa rezon ki Labank Santral ti resaman azout responsabilite pour ledikasyon finansyel avek son manda, e nou pe devlop bann progranm pour edik tou bann azan ekonomik, ki konpri sekter piblik, sekter prive e osi bann endividi. Sa travay ti konmanse formelman lannen pase avek lansman stratezi nasyonal pour ledikasyon finansyel, ki donn bann gran liny lo lafason ki nou pour promouvwar ledikasyon finansyel, avek bann progranm ki pour tous nou popilasyon an antye, ki swa bann zenn, bann dimoun aze, bann ki dan biznes e sa ki pli vilnerab. Se dan sa konteks ki sa lannen, Labank Santral in deside sanz son lapros ek formil  Anniversary Lecture . Pour premye fwa, nou  lecture  pe ganny fer an kreol, avek bann manm  panel  pirman lokal. Bi prensipal 4 sa sanzman se pour rapros nou avek piblik an zeneral e kree loportinite pour manm piblik kapab adres bann persepsyon ek konsern ki zot annan, vizavi nou lenstitisyon e sekter finansyel an zeneral. Tenm ki noun swazir sa lannen - Mon Kontribisyon anver mon Byennet Finansyel  i enn ki nou swete, atraver bann prezantasyon ki pour ganny fer, ava aport en pe plis konesans lo bann prodwi e servis finansyel, rol ki bann azan dan sa sekter i zwe, e responsabilite ki sakenn de nou i annan pour asir nou byennet finansyel. Title: Acceptance Speech - Central Bank Governor of the Year Commendation Award
text: Speech to be delivered by Ms. Caroline Abel, Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS), on the occasion of the official announcement and launch of the VISA/ MASTERCARD payment channel for Government E-services Tuesday 19th May 2015 at 11hOO Venue - STC Hall Good Morning. I am honoured to address you today at this mornings launching ceremony of the Government of Seychelles very own electronic payment channel, which is an important component of our ease of doing business agenda with the underlying objective to boost private sector growth. I would describe the introduction of this system as a symbolic milestone in the modernization process of our national payment structure as well as a compelling example of public-private collaboration as the Ministry of Finance, Trade and the Blue Economy, the Department of Information and Communications Technology and Barclays Bank came together to put this E-service in place. In view of the latter, I would like to encourage all financial institutions to join this modernization effort as at the end of the day, it is our clients and ultimately the economy as a whole that would benefit from an efficient movement of financial flows. The financial system therefore needs to be attentive at all times to the economys requests for financial innovation which will improve inclusiveness to the array of financial services. i The enactment of a more modern National Payment System legislation last year has set the foundations for the introduction of new and innovative payment services whilst at the same time setting out the rules for a disciplined environment on the part of those offering such services as customer protection is paramount. In recent times, the Central Bank has been implementing a series of reforms aimed at improving all payment-related activities, processes, mechanisms, infrastructure and users on a national level through technological means. Allow me to outline what has happened thus far and what is being anticipated. Until this point, we have introduced a number of facilities such as the Electronic Cheque Clearing system as well as the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer which the latter, we are currently implementing in phases. The upcoming phase will allow for end consumers accessing the system to make payments in the comfort of their own homes and business premises and we anticipate to go live with this phase in the second half of 2016. Another important project that we are currently working on is the introduction of a local switch which will facilitate the routing of card transactions for clearing and local settlement in Seychelles itself which will potentially allow for cost reduction and further encourage users to make the most of the card medium for payments. The introduction of a Real Time Gross Settlement System is also being envisaged, which will allow for the real-time clearing of transactions, by removing the waiting period usually imposed on payments, thereby allowing customers to access their funds more promptly. 2 With all of these projects, we will be working in very close collaboration with all of you as it is important that we meet your expectations. Ladies and Gentlemen, I wish to congratulate the Government on taking this step forward, as well as all the stakeholders for their work to arrive at the implementation of the system we are launching today. The Central Bank is fully committed to continue working with you to usher in a new phase for our financial system. Thank you. 3

Title: Opening Remarks - Second Open Discussion on Praslin
text: Remarks by Governor Caroline Abel Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarships Award Presentation Tuesday 17 August 2021 Guy Morel Training Room, Central Bank Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship Awardees, Parents Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship Committee Members Colleagues, Good morning. For the 2020 scholarship award, the quality of applications received was very high and the Scholarship Committee carefully scrutinised each application to ensure that the best candidates were selected. Ultimately, out of three applications for undergraduate studies and four applications for postgraduate studies, the final choice was made, in favour of Ms Priya Chavda and Mr Ryan Bradburn. Unfortunately, we then saw the world come to a standstill, which resulted in the difficult decision to defer the scholarship offer to this year. Education is one of the key areas that remains greatly challenged, with disruptions to how learning takes place and learners adapting to the implemented solutions, such as remote learning. Despite the challenges of the ongoing pandemic, we are fortunate to be here today for this event. The Central Bank has long recognised that it has a role to play in creating opportunities for the youth to develop their abilities and skills for the world of work. Our first Central Bank Governor, the late Mr Guy Morel, was a fervent advocate of capacity building and skills development, and it is only apt that this scholarship programme honours his name. There is currently a talent gap for certain positions in the Financial Services sector and we recognise the massive potential in our youth, where innovation and creative thinking can be developed through specialised training opportunities. Hence, this scholarship scheme intends to bridge that gap by offering, annually, two young professionals the opportunity to develop to their full potential and contribute to enhancing the local talent pool of professionals in the financial sector. The first recipient of this scholarship to complete her postgraduate studies has made us, as the sponsor, immensely proud through her excellent performance on her chosen programme. This goes to show as small as we are as a country, there is no limit to the heights that we can rise when we decide to seize all the opportunities that are made available to us. So, to end my short remarks, I address our new scholars, Ms. Chavda and Mr. Bradburn: we send you out with wishes of success and all our support, confident that you will give your very best to achieve your academic goals. You have shown your potential through your accomplishments so far and we encourage you to make the most of this opportunity you have been given. Thank you.

Title: Acceptance Speech - Central Bank Governor of the Year Award
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles CBS Board Retreat Venue: Avani Seychelles Barbarons Resort & Spa Fellow Board Members, Good morning. A very warm welcome to you all, for our annual Board Retreat. I am appreciative of your presence, for having taken time out from your busy schedules and from your families, to dedicate this weekend to a cause that we all hold in high esteem d0 that of the Central Bank of Seychelles. 2018 has seen changes in the composition of our Board with reappointments of all three Executive members and two independent members, as well as the appointment of Dr Marie as a new member. 2018 also saw the conclusion of a strategic cycle, and fittingly, last yeard5s retreat was focussed on formally initiating the process and setting the tone for our new Strategic Plan 2019-2023. For those of you who were present last year, you will recall that the retreat was also attended by the members of Management, in a bid to ensure that the process was clear from the onset and allowed the members of Management to engage and interact freely with the Board Directors and have a clear understanding of the vision of the Board and the strategic direction that the Board had in mind for the next five years. 2018 was an exceptional year. We capped our fortieth year of existence as a central banking institution, initiated activities that brought us closer to the public and kept the economy on a stable path through our prudent supervision of the financial sector and sound monetary policy decisions. Nevertheless, we cannot allow ourselves to become complacent. The global economic landscape in which we operate is ever changing and we need to become more proactive, if we are to keep pace with the developments. As the Board of CBS, it is our responsibility to be forward-looking in our planning and our decisions, if we are to provide good leadership for the Management and Staff and to the rest of the economy. It is for this reason, therefore, that the theme chosen for this retreat is d2Leading Transformative Changed3. Our strategic vision as detailed in our new strategic plan, is prompting us towards becoming more innovative in our thinking, to see how we can do things differently in order to maximise the resources that we have, especially our very capable members of staff, while remaining true to our core mandate. The ultimate goal set for this retreat is to improve the governance framework of the Board. Over the next two days, I am hoping that the tranquil and relaxed atmosphere here at Barbarons, will fuel frank and honest discussions on how we take this agenda forward and become a model in all aspects of Governance. I especially look forward to the analysis of various aspects of governance which will be presented today, in order for us to find a holistic approach towards addressing various issues and realities in todayd5s Seychellois society that can impact on the mandate of the CBS. Colleagues, I will not prolong this formal part of our retreat any further, and in concluding would like to encourage you all to participate fully in our discussions, which will pave the way for an enhanced governance framework and ultimately, ensure that the role of the Central Bank of Seychelles remains relevant. Thank You.

Title: Address - Central Bank's 40th anniversary celebration
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Capacity building for Website Developers on embedding payment gateways onto websites Tuesday March 02, 2021 Virtual Session via Microsoft Teams Distinguished speakers, Participants, Colleagues from the Central Bank of Seychelles, Good morning. It is my great pleasure to welcome you to this capacity building training for Website Developers on embedding payment gateways onto websites. Allow me from the outset to express our deepest gratitude to the speakers from various local and international organisations for accepting the invitation to participate in this very important training, aimed at cultivating the development of e-commerce in Seychelles through the sharing of knowledge and capacity building of skilled personnel. One may ask the question: Why is the Central Bank hosting such a training, and why is it so important? I believe all of us present can agree that the digital transformation of the world touches numerous aspects of day to day lives, including how we conduct business, make financial transactions and even how we interact and access information. The Central Bank, in recognition of the value of technological development in the financial services space, is working towards the implementation of the National Payment System Modernisation Strategy. Successful implementation of a modernised payment system that is convenient, affordable, reliable, efficient and safe is dependent on the shift from traditional to a more digitalised financial system. Part of this shift is in the way that consumers interact with the services and goods that they purchase. One key aspect is e-commerce. E-commerce allows businesses to transcend geographical limitations, expanding the base of potential consumers, lowering costs such as those associated with operational processes, all while being available to the consumer 24/7. In addition, it provides a great solution to the limitations that have been highlighted by the restrictions put in place in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, whereby close contact is discouraged and staying at home unless necessary to go out is becoming the norm. Efficiencies created by removing the time and cost of travel, facilitating comparison shopping as well as flexibility, enhances the customer experience. It has been observed that there are significant interest and willingness, more importantly amongst our youth, to introduce online payments facilities in Seychelles. However, it should be noted that the development of e-commerce is dependent on having the appropriate skilled personnel. Gaps have been identified whereby the average website developer often does not have the competence or awareness to integrate payment solutions within websites. Hence, these specialist services may be sub- contracted, leading to high margins and increasing costs to the client. With the appropriate training, we believe that local website developers will be better aware of the options available and will have the technical capacity to integrate these payment platforms within websites, and as such, potentially contributing to the ease of access to goods and services and reducing the cost to the customer. The website developers will also be in a position to promote the use of these platforms to clients. In line with the Governments digital economy agenda, CBS National Payment System modernisation plan and the soon-to-be National FinTech Strategy, we see this training as a great opportunity where knowledge and ideas can be shared, experience exchanged, and human networks established. We hope that this three-day training will empower you with the necessary knowledge and skills to further your interest to adopt e-commerce platforms. We look forward to your active participation with us on this digital journey. Thank you.

Title: High Level Investment Forum - Governor's Opening Remarks
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles High Level Investment Forum Monday 16 December 2019 Venue: Guy Morel Training Room, Central Bank of Seychelles World Bank Representatives, Mr Bernard Murira, Mr Livingstone Morrison and Mr Shinya Tamada, Fellow Members of the Board of Directors of CBS, Members of the Investment Committee, Staff members of CBS, Good morning and welcome to this edition of the High-Level Investment Forum. On behalf of the Central Bank of Seychelles, I would like to extend a warm welcome to the World Bank team, who will be leading the presentations and discussions over the next two days. Small economies, such as ours, need to coexist and often be on par with developments of bigger economic powerhouses. Capacity remains a challenge for our small pool of experts, who need to constantly update their 1 knowledge in a bid to propose a sound approach to the management of the countrys reserves. As such, we are grateful for the assistance provided by the World Bank under its Reserves Advisory and Management Program, RAMP, which is even more meaningful as this years team includes an ex- Deputy Governor from the Bank of Jamaica, who we hope will bring the added benefit of the perspective of another small economy. At the heart of the various topics to be covered during this forum, lies one of the core mandates of the Central Bank, which is to safeguard and ensure the proper management of the countrys foreign exchange reserves. We recognise that in order to achieve this important task, we need to continuously improve the institutions governance framework. It is for this reason that we remain committed to enhancing the capacity of the Banks staff, from those who work on the technical aspects right through to the management level where the decisions are taken. As such, the topics of discussion will revolve around themes such as governance, risk management and the global financial markets. Over the next couple of days, we will have the opportunity - and indeed the responsibility - to gather as much as possible from specialists in the field of investment management. Bernard, we are happy for yet another opportunity to exchange with you and we are infinitely grateful for your ongoing guidance and support. Mr Morrison, we are pleased to have you with us and we look forward to learning from your insights from your former post of Deputy Governor of the Bank of Jamaica. Coming from a fellow small central bank, your first-hand 2 experience of the challenges we face and opportunities that can be leveraged will be invaluable. And Mr Tamada, we are eager to draw from your know-how and experience accrued over two decades of employment with the Ministry of Finance of Japanone of the worlds leading economies. The packed agenda which is before us aims to address pertinent issues that will assist the Central Bank in enhancing its ability to remain abreast with global trends and development in reserves management. I shall not keep you any further from the discussions which I am sure you are keen to start and in concluding, I would like to urge everyone to engage actively in the discussions so that this forum can be a platform for learning and exchange. Thank you. 3

text: Closing Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles High Level Investment Forum Tuesday 17 December 2019 Venue: Guy Morel Training Room, Central Bank of Seychelles Our guest experts from the World Bank, Members of the CBS Board, Investment Committee and CBS staff, We have come to the conclusion of a short but very fruitful Investment Forum. Title: Opening Remarks - SADC Banking Supervisors Subcommittee Meeting
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Inclusive Green Finance Capacity Building Tuesday 25th August 2020 Virtual Training The Deputy Executive Director of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion, Mr Norbert Mumba Representatives from the Alliance for Financial Inclusion Representative of the Energy and Climate Change Department Staff Members of CBS, It is an honour and privilege for me on behalf of the Central Bank of Seychelles to welcome you to the Inclusive Green Finance Virtual Capacity Building. I would like to express our deep appreciation of AFIs supporting role to make organising this event a reality and to the speakers who will be sharing their insights, as well as the participants who have intentionally committed to dedicating their attention to attending this training. The Paris Agreement of 2015 provided an impetus towards international efforts in combating climate change. The devastating impacts of climate change is being felt across all regions around the world, leading to extreme weather events, flooding and erosion, decreasing availability and quality of water resources, risks for human health, costs to society and the economy, financial implications and risks to the environment. Climate change presents unique challenges to Small Island Developing States like Seychelles, in view that its impact is exacerbated due to our small geographical area, relative isolation and exposure. As an example, a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2014 has shown that just a one metre sea level increase in Seychelles could submerge many of the archipelagos low-lying coraline islands and inhabited coastal areas on the inner granitic islands, resulting in up to a 70 percent loss of the countrys total land mass. Moreover, the pillars of our economy, particularly tourism and fisheries, are both susceptible to its effects. These vulnerabilities have been proven to be indisputable as we confront the effects of the COVID-19 global pandemic whereby the importance of early intervention, alignment of behaviours and policies towards a common goal and close collaboration are key. This training underscores the commitment of the Central Bank towards broadening our understanding of Green Finance so as to make informed policy decisions that will contribute towards reducing climate risk and achieving sustainable finance. In discharging our responsibilities towards financial stability, we are in a strategic position to support the development of green finance models, thereby aligning finance with sustainable development. Green Finance is a rapidly evolving policy area that is relatively new to the Central Bank and as such we are cognisant of the challenges that we may face in the implementation of this initiative. Accordingly, this training is opportune as it will provide participants with the appropriate knowledge which will lead to the formulation of informed policy decisions addressing the 4P Framework of Inclusive Green Finance namely provision, promotion, protection and prevention. While many colleagues have a good understanding of climate change, the concept of green finance is one that is yet to become mainstream. Over the course of this training, we will have the opportunity to understand the impacts of climate change and environmental degradation on financial stability and key policy considerations that must be made thereto. The Energy and Climate Change Department will share policies adopted by the Seychelles Government. In that respect, Seychelles has put climate change at the center of its sustainable development strategy, addressing both mitigation and adaptation measures. We look forward to the active participation of the Central Bank in contributing to these measures. The Reserve Bank of Fiji and the Central Bank of Sri Lanka will share their journeys. As island nations, they are well-placed to understand the exigencies of Seychelles, and we look forward to the insights that will be presented. At this juncture, I would like to express a few words to the participants of this training. Colleagues, through these sessions, you will deliberate on Green Finance and work towards the formulation of an action plan outlining the development and implementation of Inclusive Green Finance in Seychelles. Whilst green finance is a new concept to the Central Bank, we need to look beyond the simpler option of relegating it to sustainable lending. We must advocate a holistic approach which includes public policies that promote a green economic transformation towards low carbon, sustainable and inclusive pathways, in close collaboration with all relevant local agencies. These principles could be considered within our fintech strategies and within our work towards modernising payment systems, amongst other initiatives. As the training unfolds, I encourage you to keep in mind that as representatives of your respective departments, your current and ongoing participation is key in the formulation of the green finance agenda going forward. I urge you to consider how to apply the principles that you will learn today in your various roles. In concluding, I wish you all fruitful deliberations and hope that you make the most of this opportunity. Thank you.

Title: Governor's Opening Remarks - Bank Failure Simulation Workshop
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor - Central Bank of Seychelles Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship 2022 Award Presentation Thursday March 24,2022 Guy Morel Training Room, Central Bank Building First Deputy Governor, Scholarship Awardee and Guests, Scholarship Committee Members, Colleagues, Good Morning and welcome to the award presentation ceremony for the 2022 Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship. This year, we had more applicants than the past three editions, which shows that the scholarship is gaining popularity and is being seen as a commitment by the Central Bank to develop local talents. We had very strong candidates, and the selection process was most certainly not an easy one. We received 13 applications - 2 for a first degree and 11 for a postgraduate qualification. 9 potential candidates - all in the postgraduate category - got through the shortlisting stage. They had diverse interest; more specifically in compliance and anti-money laundering, public finance management, cybersecurity, and taxation and customs management. At the end of the selection process comprising of an interview and evaluation against set criteria, 2 applicants attained the highest score and were requested to do a presentation before the Scholarship Committee, which explored the way they would give back to the country, their ideal workplace and how they would apply the knowledge acquired, highlighting key areas requiring change and how they propose to implement those in the short to medium term. 1 Each and every applicant deserve our recognition as it was a tough process. On behalf of the Central Bank and the Scholarship Committee, I would like to congratulate Ms Nissa Joseph for being this years recipient of the award. Currently working as a Senior Corporate Planning and Research Officer at the Seychelles Revenue Commission, Ms. Joseph is very enthusiastic about the prospect of pursuing her Masters degree in the field of Taxation. Interestingly, she elected to undertake her degree online, a new addition to the scholarship offering. Ms Joseph, I would like to wish you well in your studies. I am confident that you will give your very best as you have portrayed yourself to be an incredibly multi-faceted and skilled individual. In addition to the successful undertaking of your postgraduate course, I hope you are able to accomplish the various projects you envision in your role at the SRC. In closing, I would like to encourage other organisations to consider offering such learning opportunities to close the skills gap in the financial sector, which is continuously evolving. There is a real thirst for knowledge which we have witnessed firsthand as part of this years selection process. As the saying does - A little goes a long way! Thank you. 2

Title: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan for the Digital Transformation in Seychelles Fair
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launching of the Digital Transformation in Seychelles Fair on the occasion of the 44th Anniversary of CBS Tuesday 6th December 2022 Camion Hall Grounds Principal Secretary for the Department of Information Communications Technology, Mr Benjamin Choppy, Principal Secretary for Investment, Entrepreneurship, and Industry Mr Michael Nalletamby Chief Executive Officers, Deputy Governor, Management and Staff of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning. It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to the launch of this two-day fair, to showcase the Digital Transformation in Seychelles, organised to coincide with the 44th Anniversary of the Central Bank of Seychelles. i From its beginnings as the Seychelles Monetary Authority in 1978, CBS has evolved not only in the way it operates but also in its policy objectives. We have progressed from being a note-issuing organ to a fully-fledged central bank with full autonomy to determine the monetary policy best suited to the dynamics of our economy. Over the recent years, many of our operations have been automated to bring more efficiency. For example, the cheque-clearing process, which before took a few days as representatives of banks had to meet to make the exchange physically, can now be done on the same day through the Electronic Cheque Clearing system introduced in 2012. This payment instrument will not be there for much longer since the sunsetting of cheques locally is being contemplated, as we build momentum for wider use of digital payment methods. Our mandate has also expanded to overseeing financial inclusion developments, including the digitalisation of the national payment system and financial services in Seychelles. Technology pervades every aspect of our lives but no matter how great the technology, the key to digital transformation is processes and people. If anything, the challenges presented by the COVID-19 pandemic have created a landscape that encourages innovation and technological adoption. Notably, the usage of the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer System increased by 141% in 2020, with a further 56% in 2021. Be it for health and safety reasons or convenience, many private sector businesses and public organisations have accelerated their move to some form of digital platform over the past few years. This includes the launch of the National Digital ID, PUCs online payment portal, the SPTC mobile application and bus cards, as well as the numerous digital solutions introduced by the telecommunications and banking community. The theme chosen for this year - Digital Transformation in Seychelles - resonates with the work being done by CBS to lead the implementation of the National Payment System Modernisation Plan, which promotes a national payment system that is convenient, affordable, reliable, efficient and safe. This is in addition to the implementation of the Seychelles Fintech Strategy, aimed at modernising and digitalising the financial 2 sector through enabling legal and regulatory frameworks and harnessing Fintech to ensure it better meets the countrys development needs. We all stand to benefit from a more modern payment system; a digital financial system which will not only serve the financial sector but underpin the economy as a whole through increased transparency in payment, that should positively impact competition, minimise costs and mitigate fraud. Adapting products for use by all segments of our society, for example the elderly, would allow for their active participation in a digital environment. Therefore, we have the shared responsibility to accelerate our capabilities to remain abreast with the rapid ongoing migration to digital technologies, and better understand, manage and mitigate the inherent risks. To conclude, I call on everyone to work together to push the digital agenda, for us to become a leading digital economy amongst island states. I also encourage the public to attend these two days, not just for information on the digital services but to be onboarded onto these facilities. Thank you. 3

Title: Acceptance Speech - Election as AfPI Vice-Chair
text: Keynote Address by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launching of the Global Money Week 2019 Tuesday 26 March 2019 Venue: SITE Auditorium, Mont Fleuri Principal Secretary for Youth and Sports, Mr Fabian Palmyre, Distinguished Guests, Students, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good afternoon. It gives me great pleasure to address you today, as Seychelles joins nations across the globe to commemorate the Global Money Week 2019. The event was first celebrated here last year, spearheaded by UN Youth Seychelles, which deserves to be commended for bringing the initiative to our shores. This surely helped to put the spotlight on our small nation, as one of the countries desiring for its children and youth to become empowered economic citizens. Joining this global initiative also came at an opportune time, when we were getting the National Financial Education Strategy off the ground, with youth being one of the targeted groups. Launched in 2012, with an initial participation of 21 countries, the Global Money Week initiative has grown in importance, reaching 151 countries in 2018. The lives of 32 million children and youth in 169 countries worldwide, have been touched by the campaign, throughout the past 7 editions. In Seychelles, 200 children were reached directly, and another 400 people were indirectly reached in 2018. It is my sincere hope that the number of people reached, particularly children and youth, will be even greater this year, and in the years to come. As we speak, countries around the world are also launching their own Global Money Week activities, where the official slogan - Learn, Save, Earn - will become the buzz words. At this juncture, I would like to take a moment to address particularly the students present here today, on these three simple, but significant words. I am sure you are familiar with learning as part of your continuous formal education. Acquiring financial knowledge, however, is equally important. Learning about the various financial services and products, learning to manage money wisely, will go a long way in helping you to make sound financial decisions in the future. Knowledge gained can also be imparted on your peers, parents and the wider community. Surely you have also heard much talk about savings recently. While you may not be earning a salary at the moment, it is never too early to develop a healthy savings habit. It does not have to be big amounts. The small change that you keep after running errands at the shop for your parents, or a small portion of your daily or weekly allowances, will definitely accumulate over time if put them in your piggy bank. Lastly, earn. At the end of your school years, you will join the workforce and begin to earn a salary. What you earn is the reward for using your skills and time in being productive, to in turn provide for yourself and your families. Money, ladies and gentlemen, is not a matter of importance that should be discussed only by the grown-ups. I take this opportunity to urge the adults to not be reluctant to discuss money matters with the younger generation, as their potential should not be underestimated. Todayd5s youth can be seen making their voices heard on issues of importance such as climate change, creating revolutionary mobile applications, and sparking change in decades-old legislation, to name but a few. As one of the largest groups of people, the youth also have the ability to transform the way that the future generation will manage their financial resources, not only for their personal benefit, but also for the benefit of their families and the country as a whole. Allow me now to send a special message to you dear students present, in creole: Bann zenn, pa zanmen souzestim zot potansyel pour kree en lenpakt dan tou sa ki zot fer. Pran lavantaz bann diferan loportinite ki pe ganny met a zot dispozisyon. Devlop zot kiryozite, demann kestyon, pran kont bann linisyativ pour edik zot lekor e pran konsey avek bann ki annan plis konesans lo bann size finansyel e ekonomik. Ou pa zanmen tro zenn pou fer bann bon swa dan lavi. Mon swete ki zot partisip aktivman dan tou bann aktivite e diskisyon ki pou pran plas pandan sa semenn e sezi tou loportinite pour ogmant zot konesans lo bann meyer fason pour zer zot larzan. Mersi.

Title: Opening Remarks - CBS Board-Management Retreat 2020
text: Keynote Address by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles CBS Symposium Theme: Navigating Cybersecurity Risks in the Digital Revolution Friday November 22, 2019 Venue: Savoy Resort and Spa Our International Keynote Speaker - Dr Majid Malaika, Senior Cybersecurity and Digital Risk Expert, at the International Monetary Fund, Board Members, Management and Staff of the Central Bank, Distinguished Guests, Students, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good afternoon. It is an honour to welcome you all to this symposium that has been organised to coincide with the 41st Anniversary of the Central Bank of Seychelles, which falls on December 1st. Around this time every year, we find it fitting as an institution to meet with our stakeholders and stimulate discussions on a topic that is of particular relevance to the financial sector and the general public. This year, the spotlight will be on Navigating Cybersecurity Risks in the Digital Revolution. CBS is pushing forward with its modernisation agenda, which implies the introduction of more innovation to further develop the National Payment System and other financial infrastructures. As we endeavour to modernise the way we deliver our mandate and ensure that the public is provided with the capacity to understand newer products and services that are at their disposal, it is imperative that we keep pace not only with new technologies and their accompanying opportunities and benefits, but also with how to better understand, manage and mitigate the inherent risks. 1 Before going any further, I would like to thank Dr Majid Malaika, for accepting our invitation to help us gamer an international perspective of the chosen topic. A warm welcome to you and pleasant stay on our beautiful shores. I also wish to thank our local panellist, Mr Renny Bijoux, who will be joining Dr Malaika and myself, to elaborate on the emerging challenges and where we are - as individual institutions and a country - in our efforts to mitigate cybersecurity risks and reap the full benefits of technology. Ladies and gentlemen, It is a well-known fact that we are now living in a digital age, where technology is rapidly changing the way we go about our daily lives, be it in our homes, at work, in the way we communicate, among many other aspects. The rapid pace of technological development has also impacted the financial sector, shifting the way we carry out our day-to-day activities and transactions, from shopping for consumables online to the more complex mobile banking solutions. Similarly, the financial landscape also has to adapt and accommodate the opportunities brought about by advances in technology, giving rise to what is commonly known as Fintech. There is no doubt that technology is here to stay, and we are yet to see the full extent of the digital era and the array of potential benefits and opportunities it brings. Nevertheless, while all of these developments bring about many prospects to increase the availability and efficiency of services and products for the financial institutions themselves and their customers, which include businesses, we need to remain mindful of the risks involved. Data breaches, identity theft, email scams, ransomware attacks, are but a few of those risks that can have a significant impact on individuals and businesses alike, with the potential to create huge financial, operational and reputational risks for the targeted organisations. It is for this very reason that we are gathered here today, and the theme we are going to be exploring has not been chosen lightly. The diversity of stakeholders present also validates the depth and reach of technology in our daily lives, the inherent risks and the fact that each stakeholder has a vital role to play so that we can collectively explore and address the issue of cybersecurity. On a national level, various initiatives are currently being undertaken to put in place the necessary frameworks for our engagement with technology. The approval of the National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy in April this year by the Cabinet, to which the Central Bank was among the stakeholders that provided input, is one such initiative to provide guidance on the operational side of the cybersecurity spectrum. On the legal side, the elaboration of the Cybercrime Bill 2 by the Department of Information and Communication Technology is at an advanced stage and we look forward to its completion and subsequent adoption. At an institutional level, CBS, being a regulator of financial institutions, recognises the importance of the adoption of technology by the institutions under its purview and remains mindful of the associated risks. It is for this reason that CBS has taken specific initiatives to ensure that these institutions provide reliable and safe products and services to their clients. One of the initiatives is a set of cybersecurity guidelines for deposit-taking financial institutions, which was issued in April this year. This is aimed at providing a framework to guide these financial services providers in managing cybersecurity risks that come with the use of technology in their businesses. Additionally, CBS has set up a Cybersecurity Working Group that provides a platform for closer collaboration between CBS and the institutions under its purview on issues relating to cybersecurity. Such initiatives tie in with CBS strategy to modernise the financial system through digital innovation without compromising on security. With this, it is hoped that technology can be embraced in a prudent manner. As an island state, Seychelles does not share any physical borders with other countries. However, we are very much connected to the rest of the world through technology, which already indicates that the country is prone to cross-border cybercrime. While we explore ways to navigate the cybersecurity challenges, we need to be mindful that we cannot limit our thinking to the local setting; rather, there is a need for us to have cross border cooperation and ensure that our frameworks and practices are aligned to global standards, so that we can effectively combat cybercrime. Intelligence sharing has a key role to play in that regard. As Seychelles moves towards a digital economy and strives to develop its full economic potential, it will be imperative that we do not overlook the aspect of investing not only in new technologies but also the right digital infrastructure. The emergence of digital technologies is also creating an opportunity for skills development that we can tap into, to increase the pool of local experts. When I speak of addressing the skills gap, it is essential to note that we should not only be thinking of the immediate needs that will require the upgrading of the skills of our current workforce. It is crucial that the skills that will be needed in the future are factored into our education and training systems. The rise of technology, the opportunities this presents and the need to be forward-looking to stay abreast with developments in this field, will require that our younger generation, including the students we have present here today and their younger peers, are enticed to develop an interest in this domain. Similarly, they need to be given the right 3 opportunities to ensure that Seychelles will have the capacity to keep pace with the digital transformation. This will require a concerted effort between the public and private sector. We have already started this journey together, as you will remember our interactions and deliberation at the Fintech workshop in May this year. The collaboration this week between the banking community, CBS and other entities to highlight the issue of fraud, including cyber fraud, which is a key cybersecurity risk, also shows that there is a willingness and drive to move together in the same direction. It is important for us to have such forums to highlight the benefits and challenges posed by technology and elaborate on the need to devise policies and legislations that will allow the country to exploit the benefits that the digital revolution brings, while minimising the risks. It is equally important, however, that we do not forget about the need to engage with the general public. They need to understand that while technology brings connectivity and convenience, as individuals, they have a vital role to play to ensure the safe use of innovative solutions. The fraud awareness week, particularly the Anti-Fraud Expo taking place tomorrow, focusing on matters such as card and identity fraud, counterfeiting and the highlight of todays discussion - cybersecurity - is presenting such an opportunity to engage and interact with the public. Education and awareness are crucial elements that empower people to make informed and good decisions. Nevertheless, it is not enough to simply have knowledge. May I also take this opportunity to call on everyone to remain alert and always act responsibly online. We all have an individual responsibility to protect our privacy and the security of our personal information to avoid falling prey to any criminal or fraudulent activities conducted through the internet. In concluding, I am confident that the panel discussion that is about to unfold this afternoon, as well as the interaction with the audience, which I am hoping will be frank and engaging, will provide us with a clear understanding of where Seychelles is situated in this digital revolution. May we leave here with strong recommendations that will allow us to work towards creating a resilient and sustainable digital ecosystem in Seychelles amidst the rapidly evolving global digital transformation. I wish you all fruitful deliberations. Thank you. 4

Title: Remarks - Launching of the Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship 2022
text: Addressed by Ms. Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship Launch Grant Program 2020 Location: Independence House Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) representative, Representative of the Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC), Teachers and Students, Central Bank Staff, members of the public, hello On behalf of the Central Bank, I wish you welcome here this morning witness the launch of the third edition of the plowing program offered by Central Bank. Bann tel diskisyon i enportan akoz anmenmtan ki i pe promouvwar bann nouvo metod peyman, Labank Santral i osi annan en rol pour edik e protez konsomater, e asire ki tou kous lasosyete i annan lenformasyon apropriye lo bann diferan prodwi e servis finansyel, ki alafen i ava permet zot servi sa bann fasilite pli byen e avek konfidans. Se atraver bann platform parey kot i kapab annan lenteraksyon avek piblik e nou bann partener, ki nou pour kapab idantifye bann size ki merit plis ledikasyon e sansibilizasyon. Pour note ki sa i selman enn parmi bann linisyativ ki pe ganny adopte. Tre byento Labank Santral pour donn piblik plis lenformasyon lo en nouvo stratezi ledikasyon finansyel nasyonal ki pour ganny enplimante dan pei. 3 Pour la konmela, i reste pour mon swet zot en bon partisipasyon. Nou annan en tim ki la pour reponn zot bann konsem e kestyon, alors pa ezite pour sezi sa loportinite. Mon remersye zot pour zot latansyon. 4

Title: Welcoming Speech - Presentation of financial literacy baseline survey results
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles AML/CFT Webinar for Reporting Entities in Seychelles Friday November 05, 2021 Virtual via MS Teams Distinguished Speakers, Participants, Good afternoon and welcome. Title: Acceptance Remarks - Africa's Woman Leaders Awards
text: Opening remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles at the High Level Investment Forum 22 February 2018 Venue: Central Bank d0 Training Room Esteemed consultants from the World Bank Treasury, Mr Bernard Murira and Mr Alessandro Caillat, Distinguished members of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Members of the Investment Committee of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Colleagues in attendance, Good morning. We will also spend some time learning from the South African Reserve Bankd5s experience when the esteemed Deputy Governor, Mr Daniel Mminele joins us tomorrow. These objectives vary from, the maintenance of confidence in the Seychellesd5 exchange rate policy, support for the monetary policy stance, coverage of domestic imports and public debt servicing. I am reassured that we will make the most of these two days of deliberations on the topics at hand. Let it be an engaging process, where we can learn and share together in the Seychellesd5 vibrant Creole atmosphere. Title: Speech - Official launch for Government E-services
text: Opening Remarks by Mr Christophe Edmond First Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles AML/CFT Webinar for Seychelles Authorities Thursday November 04, 2021 Virtual via MS Teams Distinguished Speakers, Participants, Good afternoon and welcome to this webinar on AML/CFT.
