Title: Keynote Address - CBS Symposium 2019
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles CBS Board and Management Retreat Saturday 15 February 2020 Venue : Avani Seychelles Barbarons Resort & Spa Fellow Board Directors, Members of Management, CBS Colleagues, Good morning. It is my pleasure to welcome you all today, for the second Board and Management Retreat. I am heartened by your presence, and appreciate that you have taken time out from your busy schedules and from your families, to dedicate this weekend to our common goal - that of the advancement of the Central Bank of Seychelles. As you undoubtedly recall, the Board and Management held its first joint retreat in 2018, a two-day session which formally laid the foundation for the development of the Strategic Plan 2019-2023. It is therefore apt that we meet after the completion of the first year of this five-year strategic cycle, for us to take stock of what has been achieved, discuss the challenges that we have faced and check our compass to stay the course towards the achievement of our strategic goals. The theme under which we are convening this weekend, Nurturing a culture of inclusive growth has been chosen with the spirit of our strategic plan in mind. It encompasses the values that we have committed to uphold - Accountability & Transparency, Inclusivity, Humility, Innovation & Results Oriented, Professionalism & Team Spirit, Integrity, Mutual Trust & Respect. These values are all necessary elements to bring about inclusive growth. It is to be noted that our theme has not been chosen in isolation. Rather, it is in synergy with the global development movement and echoes the pledge made by the UN Member States to leave no one behind, upon the adoption of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. To be able to move towards being more inclusive, you would agree with me that the first step is the development of a greater sense of self - to be able to know the traits that make us shine, to appreciate our limitations, to have the willingness and drive to improve ourselves. Under the operative theme of CBS Board and Management embrace a culture of personal development, Day 1 of our retreat aims to help us gain a better understanding of self-care and self-worth. Consequently, the objective is to gain a better appreciation of our staff and find ways to nurture a culture that includes everyone and ultimately, develop effective teams that are solution-oriented, especially in the face of adversity. This way of thinking will not only benefit our day-to-day responsibility of leading our staff; it can also be translated into the work that we do as a financial sector regulator. We need to be more innovative in the ways through which we reach out to the public, how we make information available and accessible, and how we move forward with the digitalisation 2 agenda, while considering the substantial proportion of our population who are less comfortable with the use of technology to manage their finances. As the Central Bank, our mission is to contribute towards inclusive growth and development of Seychelles. Our policies have the ability to influence wealth creation and distribution and as such, we have the responsibility to ensure that our decisions and actions are for the betterment of all. To be able to carry out this responsibility effectively, Day 2 of our retreat aims to provide us with insights into the promotion of a culture of good governance. Having embraced the 2019 Board Retreat theme Leading Transformative Change, the past year has seen enhanced transparency of Board activities through the publication of the first edition of the Board Secretary Report covering activities of the Board for the year 2018; regular summaries of Board Meetings have been circulated to the staff, and an awareness programme on the Board Members as well as activities of the Board was rolled out internally. Additionally, steps have been undertaken to promote a zero-tolerance approach to corrupt practices in the Bank. We organised an awareness session for staff where they could engage with the CEO of the Anti- Corruption Commission and work has begun on the drafting of an Anti- Fraud Policy & Procedure. Externally, the Bank has been at the forefront of efforts to transform the way we tackle the emerging risk of money laundering and terrorist financing, notably through our participation in the drafting of a new AML- CFT Bill, scheduled to be tabled before the National Assembly. The new law, which has a broader scope than the existing legislation, including 3 giving sectoral supervisory powers to the CBS, is geared towards ensuring that Seychelles complies with international best practices and has a robust system in place to improve the countrys reputation, inspire confidence in the domestic financial sector, and ultimately contribute towards financial stability. In all of this, it is equally essential that our efforts are widely understood, thus the reason we continued to engage our stakeholders in discussions and decisions which impacted our regulatory framework as well as on issues that affected the public. We collaborated with the Seychelles Chamber of Commerce (SCCI) to engage with the private sector; maintained an active calendar of Bankers Meeting; published our Procurement Plan - an initiative first undertaken in 2018, and joined with the Seychelles Bankers Association and other regulatory and law enforcement agencies to initiate the commemoration of the first International Fraud Awareness Week to be observed locally, raising awareness on the issue of scams, which has not spared our small population. We achieved a lot in 2019, but 2020 provides us with a renewed opportunity to improve on our service delivery as well as our good governance practices. I sincerely hope that our interactions over these two days will stimulate our thinking on how to enhance the publics access to affordable and safe financial services and products, encourage the use of technology, while engaging the society at large to improve the level of financial literacy. I encourage you all to participate freely in frank and honest discussions. I am optimistic that the result will be firm decisions that will translate positively to the public, as this is crucial to obtaining the necessary buy-in to achieve our vision of becoming a Central Bank delivering price stability and financial system soundness. 4 To continue achieving our mission and vision and delivering on our objective in 2020 will not be without its fair share of challenges. However, the next two days presents us with an opportunity, away from our daily work, to combine our thinking on how we can come together as an effective team. We all have our individual roles, but we also have a collective responsibility, and I am counting on each and every one of you to contribute your best ideas to our discussions, so that we can make a difference not only within the Bank but for the entire population, which we are here to serve. May this be a successful retreat. Thank You. 5

Title: Opening Remarks - Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship 2022 Award
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launch Event of The Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship 2022 Thursday 23 September 2021 Virtual via MS Teams Minister for Finance, Economic Planning and Trade - Mr Naadir Hassan, Minister for Education - Dr Justin Valentin, Principal Secretary for Education Services, Members of the National AML/CFT committee, Vice Chancellor of the University of Seychelles, Management Team and Staff of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Members of the Scholarship Committee, Principal of the School of Advanced Level Studies, Director of the Seychelles Business Studies Academy, Members of the Public, Good afternoon and thank you all for having joined us. We are pleased to welcome to you this ceremony to officially launch the Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship programme for the year 2022. This initiative has brought us immense pride in making a small contribution to the development of the Financial Services sector and despite the challenges of the past year, we are honoured to be in a position to once again offer this opportunity to our local talents. The first pair of scholarships was offered in 2019 and since then, the first recipient of the postgraduate degree, Ms Hilary Baron, has graduated with a Master of Science in Forensic Accounting with Distinction. She was also awarded the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners Prize, for attaining the highest overall mark for the course. This achievement showcases the commitment of our scholars to the opportunity that they have been granted to making themselves and our country proud. Meanwhile, the recipient of the undergraduate degree, Ms Clara Radegonde, will complete a BSc in Business Management next year, specialising in Financial Management. Her results so far have been commendable. We have also sent off two new scholars earlier this month: Ms Pria Chavda has begun her studies for a BSc in Banking and Finance and Mr Ryan Bradburn has embarked on a Master of Laws programme specialising in Governance, Risk Management and Compliance. We anticipate great things to come from both of them. The Scholarship Committee annually reviews the scholarship policy to ensure it remains relevant to the needs of the financial sector. Last year, due to the impact of the COVID 19 pandemic, it was necessary to take on board feedback received, and address some of the challenges that were encountered, which resulted in the deferment of the scholarship offer, and suspension of the scholarship for 2021. Effective this year, the fields of study for the scholarship will be announced upon the official launching of the scholarship, which will be presented to you shortly. Furthermore, the deadline for applications by interested candidates has been revised to January 31st, instead of end of February as was the case for previous application periods. This revised timeline will allow the successful candidates more options when making their choices and ample time to complete the formalities to be admitted to a university. In an attempt to be more inclusive, and recognising that a Cambridge Advanced Level Certificate - or A level as we know it - is not the only qualification being pursued locally, students who may have sat exams that are its equivalent, such as the Baccalaureat, are eligible to apply for the scholarship. Moreover, the mode of study has been widened to also allow distance learning, provided it is on a full time-basis. We believe that this will allow applicants more choice and flexibility, especially for mature students who may have commitments that they need to consider. Scholars who choose this path, will also receive a stipend, as well as allowances for textbooks and internet connection. For those who opt to travel abroad, as usual the scholarship caters for costs associated with the university programme, living expenses and travel. Due to significant changes in travel requirements as a direct result of the pandemic, other travel-related costs such as PCR tests and quarantine are included. We continue to follow developments globally and react to these to ensure the safety of our scholars. Considering public health requirements, provisions have also been made to allow interviews with applicants to be conducted either in person or virtually. This also extends to the scholarship award presentation, in instances where the prevailing conditions may prevent the ceremony from taking place in person. It is good to note that in cases where a recipient opts to pursue an internship with the Central Bank while awaiting the commencement of their studies, they will receive an allowance similar to what is paid at the national level. Through this, they can familiarise themselves with the financial services sector. The Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship is offered on a competitive basis. Hence, we encourage you to take the time to put together a compelling application. For instance, ask for strong reference letters, and submit a powerful personal statement. All the relevant information are available on the CBS website and our HR team can be contacted for any further queries. Similar to 2019, the application process is being done electronically, through a designated online scholarship portal, on the CBS website. I will conclude by encouraging you all to seize this opportunity, if you are passionate about developing our local financial sector. To echo the words of William Arthur Ward, Opportunities are like sunrises. If you wait too long, you miss them. With this, we look forward to receiving your application. Thank you.

Title: Speech - Anniversary Lecture 2018 40th Anniversary Allocation of the Central Bank of Seychelles
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for Private Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles Wednesday June 16, 2021 Virtual via the Zoom Platform Colleagues from the Royal United Services Institute, Distinguished Speakers, Participants, Good afternoon. I am pleased to welcome you to this half-day webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for Private Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles - the second such training organised this week following one hosted on Tuesday for public sector stakeholders. The Central Bank of Seychelles would like to reiterate its appreciation to the facilitators from the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) for organising this virtual training and sharing their valuable knowledge and expertise. Despite its small size and geographical isolation from the rest of the world, Seychelles remains vulnerable to global threats such as the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their illicit financing. The potential for the countrys financial system to be used as a mechanism to finance such illegal trade should not be overlooked. 1 As you are undoubtedly aware, there is much ongoing effort to strengthen the countrys Anti-Money Laundering, Combatting the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation regime. The aim is to address several deficiencies identified in the National Risk Assessment which Seychelles conducted in 2016, and the Mutual Evaluation conducted by the Eastern and Southern Africa Anti-Money Laundering Group (ESAAMLG) in 2017. Seychelles was deemed Non-Compliant to Recommendation 7 of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) concerning targeted financial sanctions related to proliferation in the Mutual Evaluation Report. The public institutions with regulatory, supervisory and law enforcement mandates have the crucial task of putting the robust legal framework in place and ensuring the enforcement of laws. In this regard, the amended Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2021, which includes a new chapter covering the act of proliferation financing was assented to by the President, in March this year. However, the private sector - ranging from the banks, the insurers, the real estate agents, the lawyers, amongst others - also have a pivotal role to play in assisting national efforts to detect and deter illegal activities that can pose a threat to the functioning and integrity of the financial system. It is worth mentioning that there are already steps being taken in that respect. For example, several measures have been put in place in the banking sector to ensure that financial institutions know their customers before engaging in business relationships - be it with individuals or companies. There is also ongoing monitoring of transactions to detect any suspicious activities linked to illegal trade, including proliferation financing. Therefore, it is fitting that we extend this training to you, our private sector stakeholders, as it presents an opportunity to broaden your understanding of proliferation financing, the various requirements that the country is expected to adhere to, and possible sanctions applicable in cases of non- compliance. 2 Through this forum, you will be updated on the global trends - including emerging challenges such as the use of virtual currencies by proliferators to finance the development of weapons of mass destruction, and the specific risks to which our country may be exposed. You will also learn more about the various counter-proliferation finance tools available to enhance your compliance programmes. I sincerely hope that you make use of this training to enhance your knowledge, engage with the experts, and ask as many questions. The end goal is to improve your ability to effectively implement measures that will help protect our financial system and assist national efforts to strengthen the countrys ability to adhere to international requirements and standards. I wish you all a fruitful session. Thank you. 3

Title: Speech - Official opening of the Financial Education Fair
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for Public Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles Tuesday June 15, 2021 Virtual via the Zoom Platform Colleagues from the US Embassy, Colleagues from the Royal United Services Institute, Distinguished Speakers, Participants, Good afternoon. Welcome to this half-day webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for Public Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles. The Central Bank of Seychelles is pleased to be partnering with the US Government through its Embassy and the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) - an independent, donor-funded research institution focusing on defence and security studies, to organise this virtual training. Allow me to start by expressing our deepest gratitude to the facilitators for taking the time to share their valuable knowledge and expertise. As we are all aware, the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their illicit financing remains a growing concern globally. Although small and geographically isolated, Seychelles is cognisant of these proliferation activities and the risks that exist for the countrys financial system to be used as a mechanism to finance such illegal trade. 1 This webinar comes at an opportune time, as the country is currently strengthening its ability to identify and address proliferation financing risks and put us at par with international standards. Seychelles conducted its first National Risk Assessment (NRA) in 2016, followed by the second round of Mutual Evaluation led by the Eastern and Southern Africa Anti-Money Laundering Group (ESAAMLG) in 2017. One of the weaknesses highlighted in the Mutual Evaluation Report was the inadequate legal and institutional framework to implement targeted financial sanctions related to proliferation financing requirements. Seychelles was rated Non-Compliant to Recommendation 7 of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) concerning targeted financial sanctions related to proliferation. Since then, Seychelles has highlighted its commitment to address the identified deficiencies as part of the broader effort to enhance the countrys overall Anti-Money Laundering, Combatting the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation regime spearheaded by the National AML/CFT Committee (NAC). With enhancing the legal framework being a key priority, work is ongoing to amend several laws to be at par with global standards. To give an example, in March this year, the President assented to the amended Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2021, which includes a new chapter covering the act of proliferation financing, accompanied by a new set of corresponding regulations. These changes set out appropriate sanctions that can be imposed on individuals and entities involved in proliferation financing, including asset freezing, among other relevant legal provisions. These undertakings are currently under review by the ESAAMLG and will allow Seychelles to request a re-rating of Recommendation 7 of the FATF in September 2021. 2 Several other initiatives are being implemented to assist efforts to combat proliferation and terrorist financing through the close collaboration between the National Countering of Terrorism Committee comprising representatives of the relevant agencies and the NAC. There is also greater emphasis by individual public institutions to enforce the applicable laws and regulations and monitor compliance of entities falling under their respective purview. As we pursue all of these endeavours, it is vital that we build our capacity as supervisors, regulators and law enforcement authorities and broaden the knowledge of our staff. Todays training presents an ideal opportunity for us to be updated on the different proliferation financing trends, specific factors that can expose our country to proliferation finance risks and ways to better detect those threats to reduce our vulnerabilities. It is also an opportunity to evaluate the level of cooperation between ourselves as public institutions and the collaboration that we have with our private sector counterparts. Collaboration is particularly important as winning the fight against illegal activities, such as proliferation financing, can only be achieved through a well-coordinated effort of all stakeholders within our financial system. On this note, I hope that all of us present today will use this forum to enhance our knowledge, engage with the experts and learn from the best practices that will be shared. Doing so will help us achieve our aim to strengthen our capabilities to effectively detect, deter and combat proliferation financing activities within our shores. I wish you all a fruitful session and count on your active participation. Thank you. 3

Title: Remarks - Re-opening of Barclays Praslin Branch
text: Opening Remarks by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Anti-Fraud Expo Saturday 23 November 2019 Venue: Camion Hall Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Chairman of the Seychelles Bankers Association, Representatives of Commercial Banks, Representatives of the Financial Intelligence Unit, Central Bank Colleagues, Members of the Public, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning and welcome. I am pleased to be here today and honoured to say a few words. I would like to begin by thanking everyone for your presence and to the banks for being at the fore for the organisation of this event, which forms part of the broader effort to reduce the impact of fraud. The Anti-Fraud Expo being held here today is the highlight of the activities that have taken place throughout the whole of this week, as the banking sector joined institutions around the world for the first time to mark the International Fraud Awareness Week. Organisations around the world lose approximately 5% of their annual revenues to fraud according to a 2018 report by the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners. The fact that people keep falling prey to fraudsters through get-rich-quick schemes, offers for fake jobs, scholarship and loans, as well as romance scams that leave the victims financially worse off, or even to become indebted, emphasise the need to concentrate more of our efforts on education and awareness initiatives. It is fitting, therefore, that the theme chosen to focus our activities at the national level - Fraud: Know it, Detect it, Prevent it - places emphasis on awareness, detection and prevention; three elements that we find are key to helping individuals avoid the traps set by those who are intent on making them part with their hard-earned money. This fits in with the work that the Central Bank is doing with other stakeholders to improve the financial literacy of the population. Know It: By being aware of the various practices, actions and activities that are categorised as fraud, we will become less vulnerable to becoming victims of fraud. Asking questions, however insignificant they may seem, is often the best way to ensure that we make informed and good decisions. Detect It: with the knowledge of the various elements that constitute fraud, comes the ability to pick up on the warning signs or red flags. We need to be vigilant at all times for offers that can seem too good to be true, as most often than not, they are schemes devised by fraudsters. Prevent It: once we become aware of fraud and how to detect it, it becomes our responsibility to do all that is within our power to stop it from happening whenever we can. This element is perhaps the most challenging, as preventing fraud relies on our personal willingness to do the right thing, regardless of the opportunities we encounter, the pressure we face, or the arguments that can be used to rationalise deceitful actions. It also calls for a coordinated approach amongst the different stakeholders, including law enforcement. While this year we are focusing on the banking industry, fraud takes many shapes and forms and is not industry specific. We sincerely hope that other sectors will join the initiative as we are all targets and consequently vulnerable. I urge everyone to take advantage of the opportunity that this expo provides; engage and empower yourselves to be better able to know, detect and prevent fraud. What do we do once this week has ended is key. We cannot stop there. Fraud happens all year round and we always need to remain vigilant. I thank you for your attention and declare the Anti-Fraud Expo open.

Title: Speech - Opening of the 5th SADC Annual ITG and BCM Champions meeting
text: OPENING REMARKS TO BE DELIVERED AT THE SADC BANKING SUPERVISORS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING Date: March 1, 2016 Venue: Eden Blue Hotel Chairman of the SADC Banking Supervisors Sub-committee, Participants of the SADC Banking Supervisors Sub-committee, Good morning and welcome to Seychelles and this first annual CCBG sub-committee meeting of SADC Banking Supervisors to be held in our country. Part of the quest for regional integration involves ensuring that financial operations can be conducted within a sound environment to drive economic growth on the continent, setting the scene for greater economic cooperation amongst states. Central Banks in particular, play a key role in this process by ensuring that regulatory and supervisory standards are harmonised for successful transition towards the goal of integration all the while maintaining the safety and soundness of the financial system. It is an honour for the Central Bank of Seychelles to host this event, and we very much look forward to participating in the important deliberations that will take place over the course of the next two days as our countries come together to discuss ways to bolster financial stability amidst the complex operations that are characteristic of regionally integrated spaces. With the introduction of new regulatory and supervisory requirements imposed by international standard setters such as the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the issue of harmonisation of regulatory and supervisory norms in the region is of particular importance. For this reason, it is vital that we work with organisations that deal with issues pertaining to anti-money laundering and counter terrorism financing, in addition to encouraging collaboration amongst SADC member states to establish a common Model Banking Law. Furthermore, due to its ongoing significance especially in the context of globalisation, Anti Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism are becoming increasingly relevant to the work carried out by the Banking Supervisors subcommittee. I am happy to note that positive strides have been made as our efforts are now being extended to include regulatory agencies who have AML and CFT mandates to subcommittee meetings as well as SADC-organised trainings on the subjects - recognising the role of these institutions in establishing a financial system that is safe, ethical and efficient is pivotal to achieving the required standards for successful integration. Ladies and gentlemen, This subcommittee meeting is but one of the many occasions where we can come together to discuss the way forward to achieve the overarching objective of the African Union, as we look 1 first inside our regional blocks to foster the right mechanisms that will enable the establishment of a sound banking system across our borders. Through such meetings, SADC continues to monitor the progress made across member states, by compiling information to ensure that we are moving in the right direction as we seek to implement common supervisory standards, credit information and Basel core principles to name a few. With consistent progress having taken place over the course of 2015, we have no doubt that this coming year will see the subcommittee reach new heights as we work to support the undertakings of the SADC Governors at the higher level, by working on the technical level, towards the implementation of the objectives of the SADC region. On this note, I wish you all a very fruitful deliberations over the course of the coming days and a very peaceful stay here in our beautiful country. Thank you. 2

Title: Skills Allocation Launch of the Financial Education Youth Ambassadors 2021 Program
text: Opening remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles at the SADC CCBG Legal Subcommittee Meeting 24-25 July 2017 Venue: Savoy Resort and Spa Chair of the CCBG Legal Subcommittee, Representatives of CCBG Secretariat, Delegates, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning. It is an honour for me to welcome you here today, on behalf of the Central Bank of Seychelles, to this meeting of the SADC Committee of Central Bank Governors Legal Subcommittee. I would like to also take this opportunity to extend our best wishes to Mr Madera of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, the incoming chair and express our sincere appreciation to Dr Leonard Kalinde of the Bank of Zambia, the outgoing chair, for his dedicated steering of the proceedings during his tenure. It is without doubt a privilege for the Central Bank of Seychelles and indeed, for Seychelles as a country, to host, for the first time, the meeting of the Legal Subcommittee. I would like at this point to extend a warm welcome to all of you and wish you a pleasant stay on our beautiful shores. Since the introduction of this Subcommittee in 2010, we are progressively getting to grasp with the reality that the legal landscape of Central Banks across the SADC Region needs to change, so as to better reflect best practices. It is without a doubt that the task of harmonising laws of any group of countries is a demanding task, made even harder by the fact that upon our respective countriesd5 independence, we inherited legal systems and frameworks spanning the Anglophone, Francophone and Lusophone communities. Despite these challenges, the SADC CCBG has managed to find areas of common ground to allow us to move forward as a community. Our ongoing efforts to the domestication process of the SADC Central Bank Model Law is a good example of our commitment to bring more homogeneity in the law of the SADC counties, with the ultimate aim of adding value to and facilitating regional trade. Ladies and Gentlemen, The agenda that has been set for this meeting encapsulates the most pertinent issues with which we are currently faced and I do hope that you cease this opportunity to participate in meaningful discussions that will result in significant contributions in advancing the process of harmonisation of the legal and operational frameworks of Central Banks of the SADC region. In concluding, I would like to express the appreciation of the Central Bank of Seychelles to the SADC CCBG for hosting this session of the Legal Subcommittee in Seychelles and wish you all fruitful deliberations. Thank you.

Title: Opening Remarks - Afreximbank Business Forum
text: Remarks by Mr Christophe Edmond Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles at the Re-opening of the Barclays Bank Branch, Baie Ste Anne Praslin 24 April 2018 Venue: Baie Ste Anne, Praslin Chairman of Barclays Bank Seychelles, Chairman of SHTA, Managing Director of Barclays Bank Seychelles, Staff of Barclays Bank Seychelles Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good afternoon. I am honoured to have been afforded the opportunity to say a few words, on behalf of the Central Bank, on the occasion of the official opening of the re-vamped Barclays Bank Branch here in Baie Ste Anne. Barclays Bank has a long and historical presence in Seychelles, with a presence on this very island dating back to 1969. Needless to say, Barclays Bank has over the years built a large customer base here on Praslin, providing its customers with a level of service-delivery that is efficient and of a high quality. Among the many areas that we can address when speaking about banks and the banking sector in general, I would like to take this opportunity to emphasize on the role that banks play in the development of the economy, more particularly in the area of Small and Medium Enterprises. Praslin has a lot of potential for business development and is home to many entrepreneurial Praslinois and Praslinoise who aspire to have their own businesses, in order to help towards the development of their island. Opportunities for SME growth are many, especially in the tourism, hospitality and agricultural sector. However, access to funding to start and maintain a business, especially here on Praslin, remains a challenge as has been expressed in our previous discussions with representatives of the Praslin business community. Hence, banks have a key role to play and should seize the opportunity to bring about the development of Small and Medium Enterprises, in the way that they support businesses through financing options that are not only competitive, but also flexible enough to cater to the particular challenges that are specific to the business environment here on Praslin. With this new banking facility, we hope to see renewed opportunities being provided to the Praslin business community, as well as to the Praslinois population in general. Praslin deserves the best in what modern banking services can offer and as the key players in the banking sector, we need to ensure that the services we provide are on par with modern, international practices. To conclude, I would like to extend my warm congratulations to the Management of Barclays Bank and also the dedicated staff on their achievements and for positively responding to the needs of the customers which contribute to the development of the financial sector. I would like to wish the Barclays Bank Team here in Baie Ste Anne all the very best and wish them well in their quest of being of service to this islandd5s community. Thank you.

Title: Remarks - Launching of 40th Anniversary Commemorative Book
text: Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launching Executive Development Programme Wednesday 29 January 2020 Venue: Guy Morel Training Room, Central Bank of Seychelles Board Members, Management Team and Mentors, EDP Participants, Good afternoon. A new year has begun and as with every new year, there is the budding of fresh hope and renewed optimism to bring aspirations to fruition. At a personal level, we have drawn up our traditional list of resolutions to which we have renewed our commitments and resolved to be and do better than last year. At an institutional level, it is just as important to check our vision and mission, take stock of how far we have come to achieving our goals and adjust our compass in order to continue in the right direction. Today, I am proud to be at the helm of the Central Bank of Seychelles, a key institution that is most often described as professional, not just because we work in this building and have good post titles, but because of the trust that is placed in us to deliver on our primary objective of ensuring domestic price stability and our mission of contributing towards the countrys economic growth and development. The public relies on our institution to play a role in ensuring access to affordable financial services and products that meet their specific needs, while also promoting financial stability. Over the last four decades, we have surely strived and remain steadfast in our commitment to deliver on these objectives and meet public expectations. We have contributed towards the modernisation of the countrys economy, navigating through new challenges such as the implementation of the economic reform programme, which has required determination and hard work of a devoted team. 1 In the years to come the institution will undoubtedly continue to play a key role in the development of the economy and as Governor, I am determined to reinforce the organisational values that will allow the dynamic team that we have to be empowered, to see the Bank through the coming decades. To carry out this task and be able to stay our course in the right direction, we need leaders who are innovative, humble and results-oriented. We need people who are prepared to lead with their head, heart, and hands - that is individuals who are mentally, emotionally and physically engaged in doing the work. It is for this very reason that we are gathered here today with a group of young people that we believe are all talented individuals, and leaders in their respective line of work, having the potential to be part of the next generation of CBS leaders. The launching of the 2020 edition of the CBS Executive Development Programme, is aimed at equipping a new group of emerging leaders with the knowledge and expertise, not only in the technical fields that are essential to be a Central Banker, but also management and other skills that will enable them to influence others and steer the organisation towards achieving its vision. I would like to see all of you be:  Innovative;  Leaders who embrace change;  Good listeners;  Forward thinkers;  Independent and critical thinkers;  Resilient and able to build resilience; and  Able to influence others to make the best decision I would like to place emphasis on the last three qualities as they are vital in helping you navigate through the dynamic Central Banking environment, which is not spared from difficult situations and setbacks. Being independent and critical thinkers will allow you to be more analytical, creative and open-minded in your approach; being resilient and able to build resilience is crucial in helping you cope with changes and tap into your strengths to overcome challenges. When it comes to influencing others to make the best decision, it is important to note that this should be both within the organisation, as well as in our engagement with the external stakeholders and the wider community. These are but a few of the qualities that are required to be good leaders, and through this programme you will be provided with the necessary resources; trained and guided by experienced professionals and leaders from various fields 2 to further develop these abilities. You have also been paired with a mentor, not chosen at random, but one which I have personally taken the time to assign to each and every one of you. Your mentors will be there to support, advise, guide and challenge you as you pursue this programme. The content of the programme is very rich, aiming to give you a more comprehensive knowledge of the Central Banking environment and wider financial system. Emerging topics of importance for CBS such as Fintech, as well as the softer skills such as etiquette, emotional intelligence, and modem business communication have also been included. Taking this training programme seriously will not only benefit the organisation, but also your personal growth and development, and there will be opportunities for further development for those who excel. We often hear the call for more empowered leaders who are able to make informed decisions at the national level, but we need to be mindful that this will not happen unless we are prepared to invest in our people. We should be prepared to invest not only money, but time and efforts in creating those leaders - that is what every organisation and the country as a whole should be doing if we are to have an effective succession plan. The CBS is very much a forward-looking institution and one that is keen on being at the forefront of bringing about such positive changes. It is, therefore, my utmost desire and hope that you will all embrace this opportunity to be equipped and be willing to continuously leam, as leadership and learning should go hand in hand if we are to keep pace with developments. As Governor, I am prepared to be there together with the Management Team and Board Members, to support you every step of the way. To quote an American Author who has written several books about leadership John C. Maxwell: A leader is one who knows the way, goes the way, and shows the way. May you start getting excited to embark on this journey and give your very best, because I am counting on your dedication. I wish you all every success. Thank you. 3

Title: Governor's Remarks - CBS Board Retreat 2019
text: Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launch of Financial Literacy Booklet Friday 4th December 2020 Seychelles Post Office, Victoria Representative of the Ministry of Education, Managing Director and staff of ABSA, CBS Colleagues, Members of the public, Good morning. It is a pleasure to accept a copy of this financial literacy booklet, with a very apt title as it speaks the minds of many banking customers when faced with unforeseen situations. When I was approached to be present for todays event, I was excited. Excited in the sense that a lot of the messages and information that the banking community have been putting out to the public over the years, is now contained in one handy document. 1 As the Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles, which is the regulator for the local banking sector, I commend this initiative taken by ABSA to lend a hand in assisting the Central Bank in its mandate of promoting financial literacy for all. As bankers, we have a responsibility to ensure that we pass on as much information as possible to our customers, to ensure that when they engage or enter into an agreement with us, they make informed decisions that will protect their financial wellbeing. The relationship we have with our customers is one based on trust, and trust can only be achieved if we create a good balance of information on both sides, to enable our customers to enter into mutually-beneficial agreements for products and services made available by the banks. Mon asire ki mazorite nou isi prezan in deza fer kek tranzaksyon avek nou labank ki pan al dapre nou lekspektasyon, kot noun mazinen oubyen menm dir mon swete mon tin konn sa lenformasyon avan mon fer sa tranzaksyon, oubyen avan mon pran en loan. Sa pti liv, avek en tit byen apropriye, in santraliz en kantite sa bann kestyon ki parfwa nou annan konsernan bann servis e prodwi ki nou labank i ofer, 2 me pa toultan santi nou alez pour demande. Bann topik ki ganny kouver i varye e i tous en pti pe Io bann tranzaksyon ki nou fer ase regilyerman, par egzanp bann kriter pour kalifye pour ganny en loan e lafason ki lentere Io sa loan in ganny kalkile; bann diferan kart banker ki annan - parey credit ek debit; e menm en pti pe  tips lo kimanyer pour zer ou finans. E parey mon mansyonnen dan mon lentrodiksyon dan sa pti liv, mon ankouraztou dimoun pour servi sa lenformasyon de baz kin ganny mete a zot laporte, ki mon swete ava fer zot pli konfidan pour enterakte avek zot labank. Mersi. 3

Title: Opening Remarks - SADC CCBG Legal Subcommittee
text: Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles Launch Event of The Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship 2022 Thursday 23 September 2021 Virtual via MS Teams Minister for Finance, Economic Planning and Trade - Mr Naadir Hassan, Minister for Education - Dr Justin Valentin, Principal Secretary for Education Services, Members of the National AML/CFT Committee, Vice Chancellor of the University of Seychelles, Management Team and Staff of the Central Bank of Seychelles, Members of the Scholarship Committee, Principal of the School of Advanced Level Studies, Director of the Seychelles Business Studies Academy, Members of the Public, Good afternoon. The name Guy Morel has not been attributed to this scholarship programme by chance. Mr Guy Morel was not only the founder of what the Central Bank of Seychelles is today, but he was also an educator and an ardent believer in cultivating local talents and developing home-grown expertise. The hundred- percent-Seychellois staff rate of CBS is testimony to the seeds sown by Mr Morel. When we first introduced our scholarship programme in 2018, it was done in the spirit of building local expertise in the financial sector. This remains the key objective for the 2022 edition of this scholarship. In the wake of the pandemic, where the importation of foreign expertise in most sectors has been challenging, we have been further reminded of the importance of building our own capacity, if we are to successfully weather the storms that will surely continue to test our resilience. One of the wisdoms from Mr Guy Morel that we, at the CBS, still uphold today, is that we believe in training people, arming them with skills to make them professionals, good citizens and complete persons. With this parting wisdom, I am honoured to officially launch the 2022 edition of the Guy Morel High Achievement Scholarship. Thank you.

Title: Remarks - Launching of the CBS Executive Development Program
text: Remarks by Ms Caroline Abel Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles On the occasion of the launching of the 40th Anniversary Commemorative Book Friday November 29, 2019 Venue: CBS Building, Victoria Minister, Board Member Distinguished Guests, CBS Colleagues, Good afternoon. It is a pleasure to welcome and address you on this special occasion. Today, we are officially marking the end of the Bankd5s 40th anniversary celebrations through the launching of a commemorative book, which depicts the Central Bankd5s evolution over the past four decades. On December 1, 1978, the Seychelles Monetary Authority was established, laying the foundation for the Central Bank that we all know today. It has been an interesting and enriching journey, to say the least! We have overcome numerous trials to accomplish countless triumphs. Those of us who have been here longest can attest to the great strides we have made, both in terms of technological progress and human resource development. We have not done so for ourselves only, but rather for the betterment of the financial sector and country as a whole, as envisioned by the first Governor Mr. Guy Morel. This book is not a literature piece, but is one that showcases the aspiration, vision and team spirit of the people who have always been and remain the backbone of this institution. I am hopeful that it will also serve as reference on the core symbols that define the Central Bank of Seychelles, not only for the CBS family, but also for our stakeholders and the general public. I will not go into the details of the book, but rather allow you to discover its content for yourselves with the help of a video, which will be played shortly. It has taken us a few years to research and compile the book; and we would not have been able to achieve this goal without the support of some key people and organisations, who are here as our distinguished guests today. At this juncture, I would like to extend a special thank you to everyone who have contributed towards the realisation of this project. Dear colleagues, I am proud of what we have accomplished over the years. These successes, however, are not due to chance, but to the hard work and dedication of each and every one who has been part of the Banque Centrale team. I take this opportunity to thank all the employees, former and current, for their loyalty, their continuous commitment and their professionalism, which I must emphasize, are of great importance. I would like to express my sincere thanks to both of you for your dedication to your work. We have accomplished a lot, but the week is still very long. The challenges ahead of us never diminish, or become easier. Let's keep in mind that our institution remains an important pillar in the Seychelles economy and members of the public expect a lot from us. Every day that we enter this building, we need to give the best of ourselves for the benefit of our country first and that this effort leads to a better economic and financial environment that is transmitted to a better standard of living for everyone. I have no doubt that we will accomplish a lot more in the coming years. I hope that we will continue to work together as a team and come with more innovative spirit to ensure the success of the Central Bank and the prosperity of the country in general. To finish, I say thank you again to both of you for your efforts and hard work; let's continue to persevere in our work. Thank you for your attention.

Title: Opening Remarks - Webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for the Private Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles
text: Speech to be delivered by Caroline Abel, Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles during the opening ceremony of the SADC Payment System Annual Regional Conference July 14 - 15, 2015 Venue: Savoy Mr. Tim Masela - Chairperson of the Payment Systems Subcommittee, Country Leaders and Representatives of the Payments Systems Subcommittee, Members of the SADC ICT Subcommittee, Members of the SADC Payment System Project Team, Members of the SADC Banking Association, Members of the SADC Secretariat, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning and welcome to Seychelles for the SADC Payment System Projects Annual Regional Conference. The Central Bank of Seychelles is truly honoured to host this event; one, which we do not doubt, will spur significant and meaningful discussions about the development of technologically driven payment systems that aim to further 1 facilitate payment processes to support and strengthen our evolving financial systems. With fast paced socio-economic developments occurring worldwide especially within the African community, creating an increasing need for efficient and speedy transactions, the implementation of the SADC Integrated Regional Electronic Settlement System (SIRESS) is an event worthy of acknowledgement. This mechanism is crucial to facilitating intra-regional trade, by putting in place a more efficient and common payment system for all SADC member states. It is hoped that this will also support harmonisation in areas of common interest such as trade tariffs and border controls, which would in turn boost socio-economic returns within the region, in line with SADCs long-term goals for regional integration. Regional integration is becoming more and more relevant now that the single Free Trade area is being promoted through the Tripartite Summit of the leaders of SADC, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA), and the East African Community (EAC). This will foster greater intra-regional trade across a much larger region. 2 Seychelles is highly supportive of such initiatives including the implementation of SIRESS. While we undertake the necessary processes to modernise our national payment system with significant reforms in our legal framework and automation systems over the past four years, we look forward to joining this important regional initiative in the near future. Allow me to brief you, ladies and gentlemen, on key developments in the Seychelles national payment systems. In April this year, the Central Bank of Seychelles received Technical Assistance from the International Monetary Fund to assess the risks associated with the major payment systems against the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PMFIs). The aim of this assessment was to enhance the safety and efficiency of the payment, clearing and settlement mechanisms in the country. In the same month, the Central Bank licensed the first mobile money payment service in Seychelles. In May, the Government, in partnership with a local bank launched a VISA/Mastercard Payment channel for Government E-Services, earning Seychelles a reputation as one of the top countries for e-government development within the African region based on a study by the United Nations. The Central Bank has also implemented the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer 3 in 2013 and the Electronic Cheque Clearing System in 2012 which allow for transactions to be effected in a timelier manner. All these developments have been strengthened through the enactment of a new Payment Systems law in 2014. The latter mandates the Central Bank to regulate and oversee the national payment system for the purpose of ensuring its safe, secure, efficient and effective operation. These developments all attest to Seychelles commitment to modernising its domestic payment system in order to create an environment which is conducive to regional integration. Ladies and Gentlemen, This workshop presents us with an opportunity today, to come together to share our experiences, our concerns, and in turn learn more about the recent developments that have been taking place within our own jurisdictions to strengthen our payment systems landscape. Through dialogue over the next few days, it is hoped that we can identify any existing gaps that we need to address in order to bring us one step closer towards regional integration. 4 On behalf of the Central Bank of Seychelles and the participants present today, I would like to thank all partners involved in the organisation of this Conference. I would also like to take this opportunity to congratulate the SADC Payment System Subcommittee, currently under the chairmanship of Mr. Tim Masela, the project leader for the SADC Payment System Project, for their efforts and advancements made towards implementing the integration of the payment system within the SADC region. On this note, I wish you all a very fruitful exchange over the coming days. Thank you. 5

The Strategy, spearheaded by the Central Bank and FSA, provides a coordinated and focused approach to financial education in Seychelles. It aims to empower consumers by increasing their knowledge and understanding of various financial products that are available, and provide them with the necessary information to enable them to make informed decisions that will - at the individual level - improve their financial wellbeing and ultimately, contribute towards the economic growth and financial stability of our country. The financial services sector is ours. At this juncture, I would like to emphasise that the responsibility to ensure a stable financial services sector does not rest only on the Central Bank and the Financial Services Authority, who, together, oversee and supervise this sector. The responsibility also rests on the organisations who offer financial services, to do so with integrity and professionalism. And most importantly, it is the responsibility of each and every individual who interact with this sector to equip themselves with the necessary skills and knowledge. Through the Steering Committee for the National Financial Education Strategy, the private sector has joined together with government departments, in an engagement to undertake initiatives that will reinforce financial education in the country. This fair, the first of its kind and certainly not the last, bears testimony to the commitment of all parties involved. Title: Opening Remarks - Webinar on Countering Proliferation Finance for the Public Sector Stakeholders in Seychelles
text: Remarks by Ms. Caroline Abel, Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles, at the opening ceremony of the 5th SADC Annual IT Governance and Business Continuity Management Champions Meeting NEW CBS LOGO SEPTEMBER 2011 (3) 18th-21st August 2015 Venue d0 Savoy Resort and Spa Distinguished Participants, Good morning and welcome to Seychelles. It is a privilege for the Central Bank of Seychelles to host the 5th SADC Annual IT Governance and Business Continuity Management Champions meeting which will take place over four days. Information and Communications Technology (ICT) play a prominent role in enabling economic growth in our respective countries: ICT is used to facilitate workflows, thus allowing for more to be done in less time and lowering cost of doing business. Within the SADC region, central banks continue to exploit the benefits of ICT. As an example, by the end of this year, SADC central banks will be employing the use of ICT to allow for online meetings to be conducted; something which will no doubt greatly enhance networking opportunities. Unfortunately, criminals continue to take advantage of electronic resources and as such, new threats to the business environment have emerged over the years in the form of cybercrimes such as phishing, denial of service, malicious programs and inappropriate use of computer resources. These challenges disrupt our daily operations, reinforcing the need for a sound business continuity and information security framework to minimise the effects of such disruptions. It is no longer acceptable that once an ICT system has been installed, it is left alone to work with minimal intervention. Such systems are vulnerable to attacks both; internally and externally; they deteriorate over time; software becomes obsolete, hardware age and suffer from wear and tear, and even processes become old and inefficient as new and more efficient ways of doing things are discovered. Appropriate processes therefore need to be in place to ensure that obsolete software is properly disposed of, hardware stripped and software/hardware modernised. It is for this reason that organisations, including central banks, have an obligation to pre-empt and effectively manage such risks. The enactment of relevant laws, education for ICT users, training of IT personnel and implementation of a governance framework are important to ensure that ICT systems are properly managed and remain aligned to the business strategy. At this juncture, I wish to draw your attention to the best practices which will be alluded to in this meeting. On their own, best practices are not a solution; their effectiveness depends very much on how they are being implemented and updated. Hence, I would like to urge all participants to be guided accordingly. It is our hope that you seize this opportunity to share your experiences and knowledge on pertinent topics, while exploring the answers to common challenges that arise with increased use of ICT. Ladies and Gentlemen, on behalf of the Central Bank of Seychelles, I wish you all fruitful deliberations and a pleasant stay. Thank you.

Title: Address - Business Fair and Financial Education Allowance for Prosperous Islands
text: Speech by Ms Jenifer Sullivan Second Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Seychelles at the AFI 10th Anniversary Commemoration Dinner 10 May 2018 Venue: Conakry, Guinea Honourable Governor of the Central Bank of Guinea, Executive Director of AFI, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen It is my honour and pleasure to address you as we celebrate this year the tenth anniversary of the creation of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion. tenth anniversary of the creation of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion. My personal involvement with the network started in February 2014 where myself and my colleague Liz who is also here tonight, learnt about AFI in a workshop on mobile banking services organised by AFRITAC East and South, in Mauritius. Cognisant that most of the attendees were members of this network, and seeing how they were benefiting, we initiated the discussions, which lead to the Central Bank of Seychelles becoming a member in August. A year after, AFI attained its independence, aimed principally at reaching stronger legitimacy, and which is a model that is thriving with the support of its members and partners. On this auspicious occasion, we are provided with the opportunity to look back on the path that we have traced up to this point - our successes and our challenges - as well as the opportunity to define the path that we would like to follow for at least the next decade. Over the course of these four years, we have seen clear benefits of being associated with AFI. We have been active in our participation in the network and the Central Bank of Seychelles is currently a member of three of the 6 working groups, notably Consumer Empowerment and Market Conduct; Digital Financial Services and SME Finance. Of note, we co-hosted the 8th SME Finance and 13th Consumer Empowerment and Market Conduct Working Group Meetings in March 2017. The Central Bank of Seychelles has also benefited from an AFI Grant, which enabled a peer learning exchange programme on financial inclusion strategies. Moreover, we have been able to raise the issue of de-risking through the forums organised by AFI, in an attempt to find solutions for this problem which poses as a threat to the progress made thus far in financial inclusion. 1 The Central Bank of Seychelles has become more proactive on financial inclusion matters since joining AFI. For instance, together with the non-bank financial regulator, a baseline survey on financial literacy was commissioned in 2016, to measure the level of financial literacy amongst the population and provide an assessment of the needs including the identification of possible target groups and the main issues to be dealt with in future financial education interventions. Moreover, in 2017 we made our first commitments under the Maya declaration focussing on 3 areas; financial education, consumer protection and digital financial services. We are pleased to note that one of the targets has since been achieved, that is, to formulate a national strategy on financial education by December 2017, for which its implementation is ongoing and success will be achieved through the collaborative effort of all relevant partners. Also, the participation of Seychelles Ministry of Business Innovation as an associate member since 2017, demonstrates that as a country we are furthering our involvement with AFI. It is also important to note that the benefits that Seychelles has gained are not limited to the good working relationship, but also extends to the close ties of friendship that have developed between the staff of the Central Bank of Seychelles and their counterparts within the network. The importance of the human element side of our interactions should not and cannot be downplayed, as it is through our staff that we are able to drive the network and make it work for us. AFI has grown over the past decade and while at an individual country level, we have achieved notable milestones, we still have much to look forward to in the future. It cannot be emphasised enough that AFI is our institution and we play a significant role in driving it to further success. It is therefore vital that we continue to collaborate, have the right attitude and demonstrate commitment to pursue the agenda of financial inclusion. In conclusion, allow me once again to congratulate AFI on its tenth anniversary and wish it every success in its future projects. and wish it every success in its future endeavours. There is still much remains to be done, but we are all committed to a shared ambition and a vision vision for the future of our institution. Thank you all very much. 2

text: Speech to be delivered by the First Deputy Governor, on behalf of the Governor of the Central Bank in view of the official opening of the new UAE Exchange Branch Date: March 4, 2016 Time: 9am-11am Venue: Al Nahyan Complex, Francis Rachel Street Mr Alain St-Ange, Minister of Tourism and Culture, Mr Promoth Manghat, CEO of UAE Exchange, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good morning. First of all, let me express the honour with which I stand before you today, to address you this morning at the official opening ceremony for this new UAE Exchange branch, here at the Al Nahyan Complex. Since its establishment here in Seychelles in 2011, UAE Exchange has built a very large customer base, made up of clients that see the efficiency and quality with which it delivers services in both exchange and remittances. One of 14 class A Bureau de Change here in Seychelles, this is a significant achievement in such a short space of time not only represents its strong performance within the local context in the provision of its services but also bears testament to the flourishing relations within the financial sector between Seychelles and the United Arab Emirates. In offering these two services under one roof and with a client base that continues to grow steadily, it is indeed pertinent that UAE Exchange decided to expand its branch so that it could continue to offer its services at the expected standard. Looking around, we can observe that the new premises are bigger, more accessible and more visible to the public, all supportive of endeavours to maintain the efficiency of its services. In todays globalised economy where people emigrate all over the world in favour of finding work to support families back home on the one side, and where tourism is a luxury enjoyed by billions of people annually worldwide, the role of Bureau de Change such as UAE Exchange in ensuring that exchange and remittances are carried out efficiently and effectively cannot be overlooked. These are essential transactions for all members of society. Being a country that relies significantly on an expatriate workforce and even more heavily on tourism as a prime income generator for our country, Seychelles is especially recognisant of the value of such financial services being offered locally. With its secured correspondent banking relationships with over 140 banks globally, we are reassured of the BDCs competence to deliver money transfer services globally. Ladies and Gentlemen, Allow me to highlight that the expansion of a financial service provider in Seychelles also represents an important step in the expansion of the financial services sector in the country, where we are seeing a rise in the number and quality of services provided, that in turn contributes to our economys growth and supports our participation in the global financial market. On this note, I would like to extend my warm congratulations to the UAE Exchange and I wish you continued success in your business and operations here in Seychelles. Thank you.
